findings.title: A single click does not fully unsubscribe watched or tracked topics
findings.body: When the user's level is tracking or watching, this branch sets it to regular rather than muted. Regular users can still receive notifications for direct replies and mentions, so the email's promise to stop notifications is not fulfilled by one click. Set the topic to muted for this unsubscribe action, or change the feature's behavior and wording to make the partial downgrade clear.

findings.title: Direct save bypasses notification-level change handling
findings.body: Saving the level directly skips the invariants in `TopicUser.change`: it does not set `notifications_changed_at` or mark the reason as `user_changed`, and it does not publish the level change to other open clients. In particular, a record whose reason is still nil can be auto-tracked by `TopicUser.update_last_read` on a later visit, re-enabling notifications after the user unsubscribes. Use the established change helper or apply the same state updates here.

findings.title: The GET unsubscribe route allows cross-site state changes
findings.body: This GET route invokes `TopicsController#unsubscribe`, which changes the logged-in user's topic notification level. Because GET requests do not receive Rails' normal CSRF verification, a third-party page can send a logged-in user to this URL and force a notification-level change. Use a state-changing method with CSRF protection, or a suitably user-bound signed token for the email link.
